alt: Lung, heart, brain and muscle symbols connect through transport and regulation arrows.
A pale trachea divides into two branching airways within a pair of pink model lungs.
Arrows form a loop from a lower tissue oval through two heart-half symbols and an upper lung symbol.
A tube enters a pouch, which connects to a coiled lower tube; arrows follow a downward route.
A mauve brain model shows a folded cerebrum, smaller cerebellum and short downward brainstem.
An ivory long-bone model has a narrow shaft and wider rounded ends.
Parallel red muscle fibers form a broad middle that tapers into pale tendons at both ends.
An air-sac oval lies above a blood-vessel band; paired red spheres point down to blood and a three-sphere group points up toward air.
Small gold dots move from a tan gut space through a folded boundary toward a pink blood vessel.
A rose-colored heart model has a tapered lower tip and several large vessels emerging at the top.
Arrows form a loop from a lower tissue oval through two heart-half symbols and an upper lung symbol.
A brain symbol connects by arrows to a vertical spinal-cord bar and then to a red muscle symbol.
Small gold dots move from a tan gut space through a folded boundary toward a pink blood vessel.
Oxygen pairs and a sugar symbol move down from a blood vessel toward a cell; a carbon-dioxide symbol moves back upward.
